_comment: Sound design as numbers. Every cue in this game is synthesised from this file at load, because
a .wav is a binary asset and binary assets are the half of this project agents cannot author or
review - see ADR-0006 and the ownership table in AGENTS.md. A tap sound written as an envelope
is a tap sound that can be diffed, tuned in a pull request, and argued about.
Deliberately NOT under data/tuning/. Tuning::LoadAll reads every file there and stamps the lot
into the hash that ADR-0003 writes into replays, so putting sound design in it would mean
re-recording every replay because somebody brightened a hammer.
The four taps are a mechanic, not a garnish: 02-climbing-system.md requires them to be
distinguishable on laptop speakers, in mono, at low volume, and to differ on the attack and
decay envelope rather than on timbre alone. The decayMs figures are that document's own.
_levelsComment: Every one-shot used to play at full scale — the synthesis clamps to +-1.0 and nothing turned it down — so a tap, a hammer blow and a boot on a rung were all as loud as the game could make them. These are the levels they play at, in dB, under the player's own volume setting (F1).
_climbComment: AUD-004. The ascent is 'wind, breathing, hammer, rope, and a distant town. Do not fill it' (12-audio-design.md). A knock of boot or hand on each rung, a creak of rope per turn laid, a breath that quickens as nerve goes, and the slide down — which camera-and-feel says players should love doing, and which was silent.

breath._comment: One breath, in and out, looped. Its rate follows the nerve band — calm is four seconds, the worst band under one and a half — and its level rises as nerve goes. The nerve arc already breathes on screen at the same rate, which is the visual fallback rule 8 asks for.

_gustComment: The 1.2 s pre-roll. 10-failure-and-difficulty.md allows a gust to blow you off ONLY if this played first, so it is a mechanic with a duration fixed by gustPreRollSeconds, not a flourish. Rendered as a rising filtered-noise swell rather than a tone, because it has to read as weather arriving and not as a UI beep.

wind._comment: A filtered noise bed. Its level is the height mix: AUD-003 wants the ground to go quiet and the wind to take over as you climb, because that is most of what altitude sounds like.
wind._levels: Was -34 to -11 dB, and at height it drowned the taps it exists to sit under: the first player to hear it called it way too loud. Now 13 dB down, so a tap (-6 dB peak) stands 18 dB clear of the wind at the top.

_fellComment: The felling - FELL-003. The design says sound is seventy per cent of that moment, and it also says every failure has a telegraph (rule 7) and every audio cue a visual one (rule 8). So: mortar ticking and a low groan while the gob is uneasy, timber creaking as a prop loads up, a bang when one splits, and then the crack, the roar, the thump you feel, and a long way off, a cheer.
